feature.title: AHA 2026 Delivers Landmark AI Clinical Trial Wins as FDA Clears Wave of Medtech Devices
feature.summary: The week ending November 11, 2026 marks a pivotal inflection point for clinical AI: for the first time, randomized trial evidence from AHA Scientific Sessions shows AI-guided cardiac care decisively outperforming standard care, while a smartphone voice app accurately predicted heart failure events weeks in advance in a 563-patient blinded trial. Simultaneously, the FDA cleared a new generation of AI-powered imaging and diagnostics tools—from IVUS platforms to handheld lung ultrasound—moving from pilot to deployable product. On the hospital operations front, Sentara Health's real-world Regard AI rollout to 250 case managers is projecting 90,000 hours saved annually, illustrating that health system AI is now delivering measurable workforce ROI. Taken together, these developments signal that medtech AI has crossed from proof-of-concept into evidence-backed, deployable care transformation.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: Cleerly's PARAMOUNT trial—the first randomized AI cardiac care study—met its primary endpoint at AHA 2026, with AI-guided plaque assessment achieving a win ratio of 2.00 over usual care and tripling lipid-lowering therapy initiation.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: FDA cleared at least five AI-enabled medical devices in the first two weeks of November alone, spanning IVUS imaging, handheld ultrasound AI, sleep diagnostics, and cervical cytology—accelerating the commercialization pipeline.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: Cordio Medical's HearO voice-based heart failure predictor heads for FDA De Novo filing after DETECT-HF validated 70%+ event prediction 24.6 days in advance, potentially redefining non-invasive remote cardiac monitoring.

articles.title: PARAMOUNT: First Randomized Trial of AI-Enabled Plaque-Based Cardiac Care Meets Primary Endpoint at AHA 2026
articles.snippet: Cleerly's PARAMOUNT trial—a multicenter, randomized study of 523 patients with stable chest pain across 21 US sites—showed AI-quantitative coronary CT (AI-QCT) guided care was favored over usual stress-test-based care with a win ratio of 2.00 (p<0.0001) at 180 days. In the AI-guided arm, lipid-lowering therapy use rose from 31% to 75% after testing, compared to 32%–47% in usual care, and fewer invasive angiograms ended without intervention (38% vs. 60%).
articles.result: Win ratio 2.00 vs. usual care; lipid therapy up 31%→75%

articles.title: DETECT-HF: Cordio Medical's AI Voice App Predicts Heart Failure Events 24.6 Days Early in Pivotal 563-Patient Trial
articles.snippet: Cordio Medical's HearO smartphone system, which analyzes daily voice recordings for lung-fluid-related speech changes, predicted more than 70% of heart failure events at an average of 24.6 days before occurrence in the blinded, multicenter DETECT-HF study of 563 ambulatory heart failure patients. The trial, presented as Late-Breaking Science at AHA 2026 and simultaneously published in JACC: Heart Failure, showed 85% patient compliance with daily recordings and no device-related adverse events.
articles.result: 70%+ HF events predicted avg. 24.6 days early; 85% compliance

articles.title: GE HealthCare Launches FDA-Cleared AI Lung Guidance and AutoAS on Vscan Air Handheld Ultrasound
articles.snippet: GE HealthCare's two new AI-assisted capabilities—Lung Guidance and AutoAS for aortic stenosis estimation—both received FDA 510(k) clearance and CE marking and are now commercially available via Vscan Air Innovation Packages in the US and select markets. Validation data showed non-expert users achieved diagnostic-quality lung exams in 95.2% of evaluations, nearly matching the 96.8% rate of expert operators, enabling bedside cardiopulmonary triage without specialist imaging access.
articles.result: Non-experts matched experts: 95.2% vs. 96.8% diagnostic-quality scans

articles.title: Sentara Health Deploys AI Case Management Tool to 250 Staff, Projects 90,000 Hours Saved Annually
articles.snippet: Sentara Health, a 12-hospital system in Virginia and North Carolina, deployed its Regard-powered AI case management platform to approximately 250 case managers in summer 2026, achieving over 90% regular-use adoption. Following a successful ambulatory pilot where patient encounters rose 6% and patients managed increased nearly 20%, the health system projects broader deployment could save nearly 90,000 hours of staff time annually.

articles.title: FDA Clears Evident Vascular's AI-Powered IVUS Imaging Platform for Peripheral Vascular Interventions
articles.snippet: Evident Vascular received FDA 510(k) clearance for its Evident Vascular Guidance System and peripheral imaging catheters, an AI-integrated intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) platform built on proprietary dynamic frequency control technology and NVIDIA accelerated computing. The system features flushless plug-and-play catheters, hands-free voice control, and onboard AI real-time image processing, with the company planning further AI capability submissions as clinical data accumulate.
articles.result: FDA 510(k) cleared; AI-IVUS now commercially deployable in US

articles.title: INOVIO's VOCERYQ Earns FDA Accelerated Approval as First-Ever DNA Medicine—27% of RRP Patients Avoided Surgery for 12 Months
articles.snippet: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Inovio's VOCERYQ (INO-3107), a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy used with the Cellectra 5PSP delivery device, to reduce surgical excision frequency in adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis—marking the first FDA-approved DNA medicine. In the supporting RRP-001 trial of 32 adults, 27% of patients in the efficacy group required no surgery for a full 12 months, with all patients completing the study and adverse events rated Grade 1–2.
articles.result: 27% surgery-free at 12 months; first FDA-approved DNA medicine

articles.title: Neurotronics Receives FDA Clearance for AI/ML Sleep Analysis Module—First to Extract Sleep Time from Existing Pulse Ox Signal
articles.snippet: Neurotronics (a Nihon Kohden company) obtained FDA 510(k) clearance for its Sleep Analysis Module (SAM), a software-only AI/ML device that estimates total sleep time by analyzing photoplethysmography (PPG) signals already captured during home sleep apnea tests—requiring no additional hardware. SAM represents the company's first FDA-cleared AI/ML sleep algorithm and will be integrated into its Polysmith diagnostic software for the NomadAir home sleep apnea testing system.
articles.result: First FDA-cleared AI sleep-time estimator from PPG signal; no new hardware needed

articles.title: AI4Eyes Completes FDA Registration for Eye Care AI Platform, Opening US Commercialization
articles.snippet: Montreal-based AI4Eyes Medical Technologies announced today (November 11, 2026) the completion of FDA establishment registration and device listing for its AI-powered eye care platform, clearing the path to US commercial launch in accordance with FDA regulations. The platform is designed to bring autonomous AI diagnostics to ophthalmic screening at the point of care.
articles.result: FDA registration complete; US commercial launch now authorized

articles.title: FDA Establishes Class II Regulatory Category for AI Cervical Cytology Slide Imaging Systems
articles.source: FDA CDRH / Lean RA QA Substack
articles.snippet: On November 4, 2026, the FDA issued a final order classifying the digital cervical cytology slide imaging system with AI algorithm into Class II (special controls), creating a formal regulatory pathway for a new generation of AI cervical cancer screening devices. This follows the real-world integration of Hologic's Genius Digital Diagnostics System—independently validated at 98.2%–100% sensitivity on 890 ThinPrep Pap tests—into routine US laboratory workflows, and sets the special control framework that future 510(k) applicants must meet.
articles.result: New Class II pathway created; Hologic system validated at 98.2%–100% sensitivity

articles.title: Stanford-Harvard State of Clinical AI Report: Wearable AI Predicts ICU Transfer 8–24 Hours Early; Ambient Scribes Cut Note Time 83%
articles.snippet: A landmark Stanford-Harvard joint report on the state of clinical AI, drawing from real hospital deployments, found that a wearable vital-sign AI model predicted patient deterioration 8–24 hours before standard hospital alerts, identifying those at risk for ICU transfer, cardiac arrest, or death. Across multiple health systems, ambient AI clinical note tools reduced physician documentation time by up to 83%, with one system reporting a 112% return on investment.
articles.result: Deterioration predicted 8–24 hrs early; 83% less documentation time; 112% ROI

articles.title: PLOS Digital Health Audit: Only 3 of 1,357 FDA-Cleared AI Devices Have Been Tested on Patient Outcomes
articles.snippet: A University of Toronto-led analysis published in PLOS Digital Health examined all 1,357 FDA-authorized AI medical devices and found that only 34 were linked to registered clinical trials, only 12 had peer-reviewed published results, and just 3 had been evaluated on patient-centered outcomes such as mortality, stroke, hospitalization, or quality of life. The findings expose a systemic evidence gap at the core of AI device regulation and have galvanized calls for mandatory outcome-based post-market studies.
articles.result: Only 3/1,357 FDA AI devices tested on actual patient outcomes
